title: renderer: fix MSAA resolve when driver lowers the sample count
body:
Closes #123478

# Summary

When a project requests an MSAA sample count the GPU does not support, the Metal, Vulkan and D3D12 drivers silently create the texture with the nearest lower supported count. `RenderingDevice` and the renderer never learn this and keep using the requested count. The depth resolve shader then reads more samples than the texture has. Out-of-range samples return zero on Metal, so the resolved depth is wrong, and everything that samples it, such as proximity fade, breaks. The reporter hit this on an Apple GPU that supports 4 samples with MSAA 3D set to 8x, but any device and driver combination that lowers the sample count has the same issue.

## Changes

`RenderingDeviceDriver` gains `texture_get_nearest_supported_samples()`, which returns the requested count when supported and otherwise the nearest lower supported count. Each driver implements it with the rounding logic it already used inside `texture_create()`. `RenderingDevice::texture_create()` calls it before creating the texture, so existing callers keep working and the stored sample count and `texture_get_format()` reflect what the driver created. Drivers no longer round in `texture_create()` and fail instead if the count is unsupported. `RenderingDevice` exposes the query as `texture_get_nearest_supported_samples()`, bound to scripting and documented.

`RenderSceneBuffersRD::configure()` snaps `msaa_3d` to the nearest supported level when it is assigned, using the MSAA depth format and usage. When the level changes, a warning is printed once in verbose mode. Every consumer of `get_msaa_3d()` and `get_texture_samples()`, including the resolve passes and the hardcoded sample count tables, is then consistent without further changes. The clustered and mobile renderers apply the same snap when deriving pipeline precompile requirements from the project setting, so pipelines are compiled once with the right sample count.

Verified with the MRP on a GPU limited to 4 samples: 8x and 4x now produce identical frames, and proximity fade renders correctly at 8x.
